key_fiscal_facts.value_text: Estimated 55-75% depending on oil price and CNOOC X factor. Structure: 5% production tax + royalty (0-12.5%) + government remainder oil share ((1-X)×32.5%) + CNOOC 51% equity returns + CIT 25% on contractor income. At $80/bbl current prices: SPGL 35% applies additionally to oil prices >$80/bbl band. High-price scenario adds 10-20% incremental government take via SPGL.

Cost recovery pool = 62.5% of gross MINUS royalty. At max royalty (12.5%): pool = 50.0% gross. At zero royalty (<1M tonnes): pool = 62.5% gross. Recovery order: (1) Opex, (2) Abandonment, (3) Exploration costs (foreign partner), (4) Development costs + deemed interest. Excess over recoverable costs flows to Remainder Oil (third tranche).

25% CIT (PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law 2008, uniform rate). SPGL (Special Oil Gain Levy): 20% ($65-70/bbl), 25% ($70-75/bbl), 30% ($75-80/bbl), 35% ($80-85/bbl), 40% (>$85/bbl) — progressive on oil price above threshold. Production tax: 5% of gross production (taken FIRST, off the top, before royalty or cost recovery).

Remainder Oil (third tranche) = 32.5% of annual gross production. Split by negotiated X factor (8%-100%): contractor share = X × 32.5%, government = (1-X) × 32.5%. CNOOC buy-in: up to 51% at development decision (carries no exploration risk). Example: Penglai 19-3 — ConocoPhillips 49% WI + CNOOC 51% WI (post buy-in). X factor set per PSC — not published individually.

Sliding scale: 0% (<1M tonnes/yr), 4% (1.0-1.5M), 6% (1.5-2.0M), 8% (2.0-3.0M), 10% (3.0-4.0M), 12.5% (>4M tonnes/yr ~30M BOE/yr). Gas: 0-3% (2-5 bcm bands). Royalty exemption: first 1M tonnes oil and 2 bcm gas per field per year exempt. Post-Nov 2011 NEW PSCs: royalty replaced by 6% Resource Tax on revenue.

CNOOC right to buy up to 51% participating interest at commercial discovery. Foreign IOC carries 100% exploration cost before CNOOC participates. Named examples: Penglai 19-3 (CNOOC 51% + ConocoPhillips 49%). 25% relinquishment at end of each exploration sub-period (excluding discovery area).
